description: One tap records that something happened. There is nothing else to fill in Yahora is a minimalist event logger. You give a recurring event a name, and from then on a single tap on its chip records the date and time it happened. No intermediate screen, no confirmation dialog, no extra fields to fill in. Most tracking apps grow into note-taking tools: nested categories, custom fields, reminders, dashboards. Yahora deliberately does not. A tag has a name, a favourite flag and, if you like, a colour; an entry has a timestamp. That is the entire model, and the design goal follows from it — recording an event should cost one tap and zero attention. That simplicity is the point, not a step on the way to something bigger: nothing here is designed to keep you in the app or to bring you back to it. What it does * Tag cloud — chips flow across the screen, each as wide as its name and all sharing one type size, sorted alphabetically. Favourites are marked with a star, which changes the emphasis but never the order. * One-tap logging — a short tap records the current timestamp right away, with a haptic tick as confirmation, and offers to undo it from its own snackbar. * Long press for everything else — rename a tag, mark it as a favourite, or browse its history. Actions that do not apply are hidden, not greyed out. * Colour, if you want one — any colour you pick, as a tab behind the chip. * History as a tree — months, then days, then the individual entries at HH:mm:ss. Each branch says how many children it holds. * Statistics — how many times each tag was logged, by year and month. Pick tags to add them up together. Numbers you read at a glance, no charts. * Backup — save the whole log to a file you choose, and restore it on this phone or a new one. * Safe by construction — a tag that holds entries cannot be deleted, so a history is never lost by accident. Old entries go only in whole months, days or tags, after a confirmation that says how many. Privacy Yahora is fully offline. It declares no network permission, so it cannot reach the internet even by accident: no accounts, no analytics, no advertising and no third-party libraries beyond Android's own. Everything you log stays in the app's private database on your device, unless you save a backup file yourself. Yahora is free software under the GNU General Public License v3 or later.
